newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE strongly criticises Yugoslav elections.
newsitem.headline: OSCE strongly criticises Yugoslav elections.

text.p: The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said on Friday it was "extremely concerned" that there had been irregularities during federal and municipal elections in Yugoslavia this month.
Europe's top security body said in a statement that there should be an independent review of the election processes.

Demonstrators have been filling the streets of Belgrade since electoral commissions controlled by the ruling Socialist Party overturned clear opposition victories in Serbian council elections across the country almost two weeks ago.
In a statement faxed to Reuters, citing its chairman-in-office, Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti, the OSCE said:

"The chairman-in-office is extremely concerned about the shortcomings, irregularities and violations of law which occured during the vote verification process, after results of the second round had already been tabulated at the polling station level, and during the review of complaints procedure."

A group of opposition parties has said it won the first round of municipal elections on November 3 in 15 out of Serbia's 18 largest towns including Belgrade, but authorities overturned the results in most towns claiming unspecified irregularities.

Reruns took place on Wednesday in several cities but were boycotted by the opposition, which has claimed massive election fraud and staged the unprecedented wave of protests against the government of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.
"It is puzzling to see that the third round of the elections took place especially in those constituencies where the political opposition had won strong positions," the OSCE said.

It added that the integrity of the entire election process would remain under question until an independent review of the election had been made and said it was ready to offer its assistance in that if required.

The OSCE's statement came on the heels of similarly strong protests against the electoral process this week by the United States, which asked Milosevic to overturn the court's decision to annul some of the original vote results.
